source_text:
Fragmentum in Psalmum 2.7
Κύριος εἶπεν πρός με Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε. Ὁ μόνος
εἰδὼς τὸν Πατέρα καὶ ὑπὸ μόνου γινωσκόμενος τοῦ Πατρός, ἡ σοφία καὶ ὁ λόγος
αὐτοῦ, ὁ τῆς μεγάλης βουλῆς ἄγγελος, τῆς μετὰ σαρκὸς οἰκονομίας ἡμῖν τὸ
μυστήριον εὖ μάλα διατρανοῖ. υἱὸς γὰρ ὢν φύσει καὶ ἀληθῶς, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῆς
ἀναλάμψας τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός, γέγονε σάρξ, τουτέστιν ἄνθρωπος, καὶ
τὴν κατὰ σάρκα μεθ' ἡμῶν ὑπέστη γέννησιν, καίτοι προαιώνιος ὢν καὶ ἀεὶ
συνυφεστηκὼς τῷ γεγεννηκότι. πλὴν εἰ καὶ γέγονε σάρξ, ἴδιον ὄντα υἱὸν οἶδεν
αὐτὸν καὶ οὕτως ὁ Πατήρ, ἔφη γάρ Κύριος εἶπε πρός με· Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον
γεγέννηκά σε.
thought_title: The incarnate Son remains the Father's own Son by nature
orientation: Cyril is commenting on Psalm 2:7, where the Father addresses Christ, and is explaining how the eternal Son became flesh without ceasing to be the Father's own Son.
pass_a_gloss: The Lord said to me: You are my Son, today I have begotten you. The only one who knows the Father and is known by the Father alone, his wisdom and word, the angel of great counsel, makes very clear to us the mystery of the plan of salvation with flesh. For being Son by nature and truly, and having shone forth from the very essence of God the Father, he became flesh, that is, a human being, and underwent the birth according to the flesh with us, although he is eternal and always co-existing with the one who begot him. But even if he became flesh, the Father knows him as his own Son even so, for he said: The Lord said to me: You are my Son, today I have begotten you.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the title; 'great counsel' keeps the source's βουλή without importing the glossary term for the righteous assembly.
rejected: the messenger of the great plan
the angel of the great will

choices.english: of the plan of salvation with flesh
choices.why: Uses the glossary English for οἰκονομία and keeps 'with flesh' literal for μετὰ σαρκός, showing the incarnation is in view.
rejected: of the divine plan in the flesh

choices.why: Uses the glossary English for υἱὸς φύσει and keeps ἀληθῶς as 'truly' to preserve the double emphasis.
rejected: Son in nature and in truth

choices.english: having shone forth from the very essence
choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of light (ἀναλάμπω) and the emphatic αὐτῆς with 'very essence,' matching the source's insistence on the Son's origin from the Father's being.
rejected: having radiated from the substance itself
having sprung from the very being

choices.why: Uses the glossary English for σάρξ and keeps the aorist 'became' to mark the incarnation event.

choices.english: knows him as his own Son
choices.why: Keeps ἴδιον as 'his own' to stress the natural, proper Sonship, and renders οἶδεν as 'knows' rather than 'acknowledges' to stay literal.
rejected: recognizes him as his own Son
knows him to be his own Son

bible_refs.note: Κύριος εἶπε πρός με· Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε

pass_b_english: The one who alone knows the Father and is known by the Father alone, his wisdom and word, the angel of great counsel, makes the mystery of the plan of salvation with flesh very clear to us. For though he is Son by nature and truly, and though he has shone forth from the very essence of God the Father, he became flesh—that is, a human being—and underwent birth according to the flesh among us, even though he is eternal and always co-existing with the one who begot him. Yet even though he became flesh, the Father knows him as his own Son even in this state. For he said, "The Lord said to me: 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you'" (Psalm 2:7).

last_rejected.why: Brief glossary maps οἰκονομία to 'plan of salvation'; 'angel of great counsel' is a standard title but not checked against glossary.
last_rejected.ruling: Glossary issue about οἰκονομία, not about 'angel of great counsel'; no error in the rendering itself.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'flesh' for σάρξ; explanatory 'human being' adds non-glossary term.
last_rejected.fix: flesh—that is, a human being → flesh
last_rejected.ruling: τουτέστιν ἄνθρωπος is appositional gloss on σάρξ; 'human being' correctly renders ἄνθρωπος, not σάρξ.

last_rejected.why: Isaian title 'Angel of Great Counsel' refers to Christ; 'angel' misleads as created being.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ τῆς μεγάλης βουλῆς ἄγγελος is standard patristic title; 'angel' is literal and conventional, not mistranslation.

last_rejected.why: Missing opening Scripture citation formula 'The Lord said to me...' that frames the fragment.
last_rejected.fix: Add before: 'The Lord said to me, "You are my Son; today I have begotten you."' The one who alone knows...
last_rejected.ruling: Κύριος εἶπεν πρός με is Scripture text quoted at fragment start, not a citation formula; English includes it later as quote.

last_rejected.why: English hides that the Father's quoted words open the fragment; voice marker lost.
last_rejected.fix: Open with the Father's scriptural words, then identify Christ as the one who knows the Father.
last_rejected.ruling: Κύριος εἶπεν πρός με is Psalm 2:7 text, not narrative voice; English correctly renders it as Scripture quotation, not hiding speaker.
